title: AI Streaming Assistant Suspense & Localized Error Boundary Fallback
businessContext: A customer support portal embeds an AI conversational assistant in the sidebar. If the external LLM streaming endpoint times out or errors with a 503, the entire Next.js page currently crashes with an unhandled server error, locking out agents from viewing customer tickets.
problemStatement: Restructure the page using Next.js App Router streaming architecture with React `<Suspense>` and nested localized `error.tsx` / `<ErrorBoundary>` components. The ticket details must render immediately, the AI assistant must stream in progressively, and an AI failure must show a retry card inside the sidebar without affecting the main ticket view.
constraints: Main page ticket data must render with 0 delay (not blocked by AI stream).
AI assistant must stream chunk by chunk inside Suspense boundary.
LLM error must be caught locally inside the sidebar component boundary.
candidateTasks: Explain how React Suspense and HTTP Chunked Transfer Encoding enable Progressive Hydration in Next.js.
Wrap slow AI component in `<Suspense fallback={<AiSkeleton />}>`.
Implement localized Error Boundary around sidebar so AI timeouts never crash ticket view.
hints: In Next.js App Router, `loading.tsx` and `<Suspense>` stream HTML over HTTP chunked transfer encoding.
Errors bubble up to the nearest `error.tsx` boundary. If placed at the root, the entire page is replaced.

testCases.name: Isolates streaming failure from core page view
testCases.explanation: Enables independent progressive loading and failure containment.

alternativeApproaches: Using Vercel AI SDK `useChat` / `useCompletion` with client-side streaming over WebSockets or SSE.
commonMistakes: Awaiting the AI call at the page root component level, blocking TTFB for the entire application.
Not providing a retry handler in the Error Boundary.
